The slant-range resolution of a high-resolution radar measurement system is approximately 0.15 m or 15 cm.
The system is calibrated by measuring a known standard target such as a sphere, a Luneberg lens, a cylinder, a flat plate, or a comer reflector.
A typical number of range profiles measured in a series is 256 profiles.
The complex radar system transfer function is transformed to obtain the complex, high-resolution range profile.
Compact ranges provide a controlled environment with reduced multipath reflections and improved accuracy.
X-band and S-band frequencies are typically used in compact range measurements.
Edge treatment is used to reduce diffraction and associated ripples in the quiet zone.
Physical scale modeling of electromagnetic measurements uses a scale factor of the ratio of the linear dimension of the target to the linear dimension of the model.
Radar image modeling system (RIMS) is used to measure the radar signatures of scale model ships in a simulated ocean environment.
The indoor water pool used in RIMS is approximately 200 ft X 300 ft in size.
Transportable van-mounted radar measurement systems provide a portable and flexible measurement system for RCS measurement.
The Naval Ocean Systems Center in San Diego developed a radar system for measuring the RCS of full-scale operational ships and aircraft.
The radar system is located about 120 ft above sea level and has an unobstructed view greater than 180°.
The system measures the complex radar return of full-scale operational ships as they maneuver within a range of about 10 nautical miles.
The measurements are calibrated against a spherical standard target suspended on a rope below a helicopter.
A secondary standard is a Luneberg lens mounted on a tower on land.
The motion of the ship is measured by motion sensors onboard the ship and transmitted to the radar site in real time for correlation with the radar data.
